The patient is a 21-year-old female with sickle cell disease, systemic sclerosis, and Crohn's disease who returns for psychiatric follow-up approximately six months after her last visit, again presenting with concerns regarding food intake and exercise patterns initially addressed in Endocrinology earlier this year.
She reports a recent change in lifestyle to "feel healthier" and has been strictly limiting her food intake and exercising intensely every day.
She avoids carbohydrates and fats, frequently skips meals, and becomes anxious when she cannot complete her daily workout.
She denies purging or using laxatives but admits she feels guilty if she eats more than planned.
Her menstrual periods stopped approximately one year ago, which she attributes to work stress and weight changes.
She weighs herself daily and says she's comfortable maintaining a low body weight because she "feels in control."

lines: Persistent pain in her left shin, which worsens with running
The patient is a 23-year-old female with sickle cell disease, systemic sclerosis, Crohn's disease, anorexia nervosa, and osteoporosis who returns for evaluation of persistent left shin pain.
She presents to orthopedics following her last gastroenterology encounter six months ago for a Crohn's disease flare.
She reports that she has been training for a marathon over the past 6 months and has recently increased her running distance.
She denies any specific injury but mentions that the pain has been gradually increasing.
She also expresses frustration about having to reduce her training due to the pain.
On further questioning, she reveals that she has been following a strict diet to maintain her weight for competitive running and admits to being fearful of gaining weight.
She has not had a menstrual period for the last 4 months.
